Slime rancher is a great game and this game is essentially the same as the first slime rancher. This is more like a visual remake of the first game but with less content due to not having the DLC. Id recommend playing the first one instead as there is overall more stuff to do.
If you have played the first one already this really does not offer much more than fresh start to essentially doing the exact same thing.

Edit: The game has improved a lot since it first came out. Still has a lot of the same issues the first game had (slimes ignoring food/not eating despite it literally being in front of their face or shot at them, gardens growing super slow despite upgrades, etc) but overall is a worthy successor and has a fun and engaging story to be told. Plus there's a fun mechanic of collecting rarer slimes which can keep you busy well after finishing the story.

Pretty good. Honestly not as fun as the original however as it feels like it takes a *ton* more work to earn money. You also start without the jetpack and it takes a long time to get it and other upgrades you your vacpack due to having to manually collect components to build said upgrades. There us also apparently no drones, so no automation yet. Plort collectors and food dispensers are still a thing, but you have to be careful about which slimes you give food automatically, as a few have unique abilities that can cause you to waste food with no reward given back! Exploring and expanding your map view is also a smidgen tedious as the map discovery beacons are kinda hard to locate in several areas.

Boom + Phosphor
Rock + Tabby
Cotton + Crystal
Saber + Dervish
Ringtail + Hunter
Ringtail + Flutter
Ringtail + Tangle

ESPECIALLY the Ringtail Hunters. I keep those ones in the cave part of the ranch, along with the Angler Pinks, Boom Phosphors, and Batty Honeys. If you're going to have the Hunter largos in the cave, I would also suggest keeping your Flutters in there, so when you feed them, the aura bursts they release will calm them down if the Hunters are agitated and/or feral.

This game is a huge upgrade from the first one. The atmosphere and art style are so cozy that you’ll feel at home in every part of the map. Grinding and overall gameplay have been greatly improved, now that ranchers can gather resources using only the Vacpack and the upgrade system has been changed for the better. There isn’t much depth to the story, but it is still an interesting and creative journey to follow, and even somewhat relatable. Speaking of creativity, it is the game’s strongest point, with beautiful biomes and environments, amazing level design, and unique slimes with distinct behaviors.

Finally, this is definitely a game you can sit back and relax with, simply enjoying the vibe of being a rancher in a mysterious world full of colorful slimes.

As someone who absolutely adores the first Slime Rancher game, I can say with complete confidence that I fully support and cannot wait for the full release of this game! Monomi Park clearly has a passion for this style and genre of game which I find exceptionally enthralling and delightful. The gameplay is smooth, the graphics are as dream-like as ever, and the new mechanics implemented are working rather well for myself! I'll admit, the expanded science system is taking some getting used to but I still find it entertaining and enjoyable to a degree. The game so far is still in early access making it difficult to say there are no issues, but issues I have with this game are completely overshadowed by the trust I have in this company and the potential for the game as a whole!

Little suggestion: with such a different landmass which may be difficult to navigate, perhaps consider implementing a mini map which players can choose to display- perhaps craft on their own- so as to avoid the frustration with retracing and getting lost. Maybe this is already a thing and I just haven't seen it yet but, if it isn't, give it some thought!

tldr.text: Very Positive (94%): players love the graphics, art and relaxed gameplay.
The main complaint is the grind, cited in 7% of reviews, with repetitive content and music drawing criticism.

details.text: Recent reviews complain far less about bugs and crashes, and fewer mention the price.
Newer players are the least positive at 88%, while veterans with over 50 hours sit higher.
